skill.name: frontend-accessibility
skill.description: Build accessible user interfaces using semantic HTML, ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, color contrast, and screen reader compatibility. Use this skill when creating or modifying HTML templates, React/Vue components, forms, interactive elements, navigation menus, modals, or any UI code. Apply when implementing keyboard navigation, focus management, alt text for images, form labels, heading structure, color contrast, or testing with screen readers. Use for all frontend development to ensure interfaces are usable by people with disabilities and meet WCAG accessibility standards.
skill.summary: Guide frontend work toward WCAG-aware, keyboard-accessible, screen reader-friendly interfaces.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a relative Markdown link that uses parent directory segments to reference an accessibility standards document. This is not executable filesystem access, and I found no prompt injection, network activity, or data exfiltration intent in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:29 contains a Markdown documentation link using ../../../ to reference an accessibility standards file. It does not instruct runtime file reads, writes, path concatenation, or access to user-controlled paths.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams often miss keyboard, semantic, and screen reader requirements during routine UI work. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to apply accessibility checks while creating or editing interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of semantic HTML for page structure and controls.
Applies ARIA guidance when native HTML is not enough.
Checks keyboard navigation and focus management for interactive elements.
Prompts for accessible labels, validation messages, and form relationships.
Considers color contrast and non-color indicators for visual states.
Supports accessibility review of templates, JSX, components, and page layouts.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not formal WCAG certification.
It does not run browser, screen reader, or automated accessibility tests by itself.
It cannot confirm real assistive technology behavior without user testing.
It focuses on frontend interface work, not legal compliance programs.

use_cases.title: Review Component Markup
use_cases.description: Find missing labels, weak semantics, and keyboard barriers before a component is merged.

use_cases.title: Improve Design System Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply consistent accessibility rules to forms, menus, dialogs, and reusable controls.

use_cases.title: Prepare Accessibility QA Notes
use_cases.description: Create focused review notes for keyboard flow, focus order, headings, and screen reader support.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Markup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small template or component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI for accessibility basics. Focus on semantic HTML, labels, headings, alt text, and obvious keyboard issues.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Form
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve form labels, validation, and error messaging.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this form for accessibility. Check labels, descriptions, required fields, validation messages, focus behavior, and error announcement.

prompt_templates.title: Design Keyboard Interaction
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan behavior for menus, modals, tabs, or custom controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define the keyboard and focus behavior for this interactive component. Include expected tab order, focus return, ARIA use, and escape behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a WCAG Remediation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a feature or page before release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for accessibility risks. Group issues by user impact, propose code-level fixes, and note what needs browser or screen reader testing.

output_examples.input: A login form uses placeholder-only labels and color-only error states.
output: Add persistent labels that remain visible after users type.
Connect errors to fields with accessible descriptions.
Add text or icons so errors do not rely on color alone.

output_examples.input: A modal opens from a settings button and contains several form controls.
output: Move focus into the dialog when it opens.
Keep keyboard focus inside the dialog until it closes.
Return focus to the settings button after closing.

output_examples.input: A page has several cards with clickable titles and icons.
output: Use real links or buttons for interactive elements.
Ensure headings follow a clear page hierarchy.

best_practices: Prefer native HTML controls before adding ARIA.
Test every interactive path with keyboard navigation.
Pair automated checks with manual review and assistive technology testing.
anti_patterns: Do not use div or span elements as controls without complete keyboard support.
Do not hide focus indicators for visual styling.
Do not rely only on color to communicate errors, status, or selection.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee WCAG compliance?
faq.answer: No. It provides practical guidance, but final compliance requires testing, review, and organizational approval.

faq.question: Can it help with React or Vue components?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill applies to HTML templates, JSX, component markup, and common frontend patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace automated accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. Use it with automated tools, manual keyboard testing, and assistive technology checks.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when creating, modifying, or reviewing frontend UI code, especially forms and interactive components.

faq.question: Does it cover screen reader concerns?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides names, roles, descriptions, announcements, headings, and semantic structure.

faq.question: Can it help with color contrast?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts review of contrast and asks for non-color indicators where meaning is important.
